Set operations (.add(), 'in', len(), clear()) work on new set type. Before build lacks .add() on dict.

conclusion.rationale: sys.lazy_modules changed from dict to set — a verified, intentional API signature change per PEP 810. The type change breaks code using dict methods (subscript, .keys(), .items()) on sys.lazy_modules. All normal-execution-path lines are covered by gcov; only fault-injection error paths remain uncovered. The test suite confirms the new set-based behavior works correctly.
recommended_actions: Update all downstream code using sys.lazy_modules from dict-style access to set membership checks.
Use fault injection to cover error-handling paths in _PyImport_InitLazyModules, register_from_lazy_on_parent, _PyImport_LazyImportModuleLevelObject, and _imp__set_lazy_attributes_impl.
Run Lib/test/test_lazy_import/__init__.py as a regression gate.
Document the type change in release notes and migration guides.
